lines: de, peut produire ſon propre frere: outre, le fiſque, où
le Roy qui ſeul luy fait la partie pour monſtrer qu'il a
commis le meurtre en ſe defendant {f}: car bien que le
Roy pourſuyue la confiſcation de l'accuſé: toutesfois
tel gain penal, & odieux qui ne peut aduenir, qu'auec
le detriment, & iacture tant de l'honneur, que de la vie
du preuenu, ne vient en conſideration. {g}
En ſecond lieu, il y a des teſmoins qui
eſtoient és nopces deſdits Martin, & de
Rols, & meſmement vne Catherine
Boëre, qui porta ſur la minuict la colla-
tion (qu'ils appelloient le reſueil) laquel-
le obſtinément aſſeure, que c'eſt celuy
qui eſpouſa ladite de Rols, & qu'elle
trouua couché auec elle. Troiſieme-
ment, la meilleure partie des teſmoins
donne des marques, & coniectures in-
uincibles, à ſçauoir, que Martin Guerre
auoit deux ſoubredens à la machoire de
deſſus, vne cicatrice au front, vne ongle
du premier doigt enfoncée, trois verrues
ſur la main droitte, vne autre au petit
doigt, & vne goute de ſang à l'œil gau-
che, leſquelles marques ont eſté toutes
trouuées au priſonnier.
Ceci me faict ſouuenir de Q Fabius Maximus, le
quel par tant qu'il eſtoit plein de petites tumeurs de
chair eſleuées ſur la peau du corps, (appelée des Fran-
çois, à l'imitatiõ du Latin, Verrues) iuſqu'aux enuirõs de
la mãmelle, fut des Romains appelé VERRVCOSVS

A pale brown stain runs across the head margin and just touches the top of the running head and the folio '61' without obscuring them. The outer (right) margin is clean; the inner (left) edge of every crop carries a narrow strip of the facing verso ('u-', 'ci-', 'd', 'ts', 'il'), ignored throughout per the crop rule. Nothing is lost to damage or to the gutter.

counts for the reconciler: 30 printed body lines in 3 paragraph blocks (7 + 18 + 5) with 2 heading blocks between them ('TEXTE.' and 'ANNOTAT. XL.', both spaced capitals). 2 markers ({f}, {g}), both in the first paragraph, each with a margin note; 2 margin notes, each with a marker. No foot citation block, no signature, no catchword, no ornament, no decorated initial. The lower third of the leaf below the last body line is blank.

continues_prev: the page opens mid-sentence with 'de, peut produire ſon propre frere' (the tail of a sentence begun on p060, which is not transcribed, so this rests on the sense alone). continues_next false: the paragraph closes with 'conſideration. {g}' and the heading 'TEXTE.' follows on the same page. blocks[4] continues_next true: the last line ends 'appelé VERRVCOSVS' with no point, running on to p062.

uncertain.text: commis le meurtre en ſe defendant {f}: car bien que le
uncertain.note: the marker is the small italic f, and the mark after it is a colon (two clearly separate dots at 4.5x), not a period. The print sets 'carbien' tight; normalized to 'car bien' per §1.

uncertain.text: du preuenu, ne vient en conſideration. {g}
uncertain.note: the line ends with a baseline period followed by the italic marker g; marker order kept as printed. 'vienten' and 'enconſideration' are set tight and normalized per §1.

the surname is 'Rols' (R-o-l-s), not 'Rois': at 4x the fourth sort is a full-ascender l with no dot, identical in height to the l of 'elle'. Same reading at blocks[2].lines[6] ('ladite de Rols'), where a speck of show-through above the o can be mistaken for an i-dot. Agrees with the small-capital 'ROLS' cited in the conventions (§3).

the print sets 'tion(qu'ils' and ')laquel-' with no space outside either parenthesis; normalized per §1 (space outside, none inside). The apostrophe of 'qu'ils' is set high and sits beside the i's dot, so the pair can read as a diaeresis; at 3x there are two separate marks, a slanted raised comma and a round dot.

uncertain.text: auoit deux ſoubredens à la machoire de
uncertain.note: two small ragged ink blobs stand between 'machoire' and 'de', one at ascender height and one below the baseline (checked at 6x on the full-page scan). Neither has a letterform, they are not an italic marker letter, and no note answers to them; read as ink specks or a piece of furniture that took ink, and not transcribed. The print also sets 'lamachoire'; normalized to 'à la machoire de' per §1.

uncertain.text: du premier doigt enfoncée, trois verrues
uncertain.note: printed 'enfoncée,trois' with no space after the comma; normalized per §1. Same normalization applied to 'destesmoins' (lines[8]) and 'desang' (lines[15]).

uncertain.text: deſſus, vne cicatrice au front, vne ongle
uncertain.note: double-s checked at 4x: 'deſſus' is long s + long s (both full ascenders, ligatured), not 'ſs'. Same check made at 'aſſeure' (lines[5]), 'leſquelles' (lines[16]) and 'deſſus citée' in margin_notes[0]; all are ſſ. The second c of 'cicatrice' is lightly inked but is a c, not an e.

uncertain.note: no abbreviation point is visible after the Q of 'Q Fabius' (Quintus). The sort is a long-tailed roman Q whose tail sweeps right under the following space, and at 4.5x there is no dot on the baseline. Transcribed without a point; reader A may read 'Q.'

uncertain.note: the last word is set in letterspaced capitals ('V E R R V C O S V S'), closed up here per §3, and the block is flagged spaced_caps. Ten sorts counted twice at 4x on both the body strip and the foot crop; the final one is a capital S, not a long s.
a small ink blot sits on the final a of 'la'; the letter is still legible as a at 6x. The note's own key letter f is printed before 'Balde' and is not included in lines, per §9.
read 'Parentes.' at 6x (the penultimate sort is an e with a closed eye and mid bar, not a u). = Balde on l. Parentes, cited above.

the sort transcribed 'P.' (twice, lines[1] and lines[2]) is a single italic capital-P-shaped glyph with a large looping bowl, standing where a section/paragraph reference belongs ('§. penultime', '§. ſi'). It may be this fount's paragraph abbreviation rather than a plain letter P. Transcribed as the letter printed; flagged so the reconciler can settle the house practice against other pages.

two doubts on one line. (a) The first sort is read as italic long ſ, not f: at 7x on the full-page scan its cross-nub projects only to the left of the stem, where the f of 'fut' on the same line has a bar crossing both sides; the sense agrees ('l. ſi cui, §. ſi'). (b) The last word is transcribed 'fut.' as printed: the final sort has a stem rising above x-height with a left crossbar, matching the t of 'penulti-' rather than the arm-to-the-right r of 'ri.' — although the citation sense wants 'fur.' (D. de furtis). Recorded as a possible wrong sort per §7(c); reader A may read 'fur.'

the line ends 'vxo' with no word-break hyphen and runs on to 'ri.' on the next line; normal for this print (§1), listed only so the reconciler does not read it as a dropped hyphen. Point spacing after 'l.', 'ri.', 'me.' and 'ſi.' normalized per §1, where the print sets them tight.

placement: the f note's first line is printed exactly beside body line 'commis le meurtre en ſe defendant {f}: car bien que le'. The g note is set some six lines lower than the f note, its first line beside 'du preuenu, ne vient en conſideration. {g}' — the line that carries its marker. Both beside_line values are firm here; the margin is uncrowded.

there is no foot citation block, no signature and no catchword: both citations fit in the outer margin and the whole lower third of the leaf is blank (verified on foot.jpg, margin-4.jpg and body-8.jpg, all of which are bare paper below the last body line).

uncertain.text: Roy pourſuyue la confiſcation de l'accuſé: toutesfois
uncertain.note: validator long-s check: 'toutesfois' is printed with a round s before the f, which is correct for this fount (§2: long s is not used before b, f, k), so no normalization has occurred. Same for 'és nopces' and 'des teſmoins'. The mark after 'accuſé' is a colon (two dots at 4.5x), not a semicolon or period.
